questions.q: Which of these must AutoInvoice be able to determine before it will create a transaction?
options: The customer's favorite shipping carrier
The warehouse's forklift inventory
A remit-to address for the customer and site
The salesperson's commission rate
questions.explain: AutoInvoice requires a determinable remit-to address — where the customer should send payment — or it rejects the record.

questions.q: What is a key difference between a "rejected" and an "error" record in AutoInvoice?
options: A rejected record often fails for a structural/setup reason without always showing detail; an error record is flagged with a more specific visible reason
They are identical in every way
Error records are deleted immediately; rejected records are not
Rejected records always become transactions automatically
questions.explain: Rejections are often structural (and may not detail the reason in the standard report), while errors carry a more specific, visible reason.

questions.q: Why was SO-48217's line rejected by AutoInvoice in this lesson's scenario?
options: Harborview's credit limit was exceeded
The order had not shipped yet
The item did not exist
A newly created bill-to site had no remit-to address assigned
questions.explain: A new secondary bill-to site for Harborview had never been assigned a remit-to address, so AutoInvoice could not determine where payment should go.

questions.q: What tool is used to investigate and correct rejected or errored AutoInvoice records?
options: Approval Management (AME)
Manage AutoInvoice Lines
Lockbox processing
Create Accounting
questions.explain: Manage AutoInvoice Lines lets users search, review reasons, correct, flag, and resubmit interface records.

questions.q: What happens to a rejected or errored record while it awaits correction?
options: It is permanently deleted from the system
It is automatically converted into a credit memo
It remains safely in the Receivables interface tables until corrected and resubmitted
It is sent directly to the General Ledger
questions.explain: Rejected/errored records stay in the interface tables — nothing is lost — until they are corrected and AutoInvoice runs again.
